hourly.summary: Manchester United fans are in full-blown crisis mode across both platforms. Forum posters are genuinely discussing relegation — a word that should never share a sentence with 'United' — while dissecting the club's structural rot: a striker-less attack, a sieve defence, an owner class deemed 'inept', and a manager (Carrick) seemingly waiting for the sack. BlueSky mirrors the gloom with calls for Carrick to 'resign and tell the truth', INEOS communication critiques, and Eddie Howe speculation as the vultures circle. The only relief is a nostalgic FIFA 99 Treble flashback — a painful reminder of what once was.

daily.summary: Fan sentiment remains catastrophically low across all three checkpoints, locked in a uniform 2/10 crisis after a 3-0 home loss to Bournemouth extends the winless streak to eight games. The mood shows no meaningful shift — only a deepening consensus that the club's structural rot, ownership failures, and managerial vacuum have created an unprecedented, self-perpetuating disaster. Gallows humor masks pure resignation: same script, different actors, inevitable collapse.

weekly.summary: Manchester United fan sentiment remained locked in a sustained, week-long catastrophe with scores barely moving from 2/10 across all seven days. The 4-1 Champions League thrashing by Como and a 3-0 home humiliation to Bournemouth bookended a period defined by total loss of faith in Carrick, the Glazers, and INEOS, with the mood hardening from grim resignation into open revolt — anti-ownership chants, serious relegation talk, and gallows humour as the only coping mechanism. No meaningful improvement occurred; the week ended in full-blown freefall.
